answer: An agent marketplace allows one daily bid per public key while that key has $100 locked in a 30-day escrow. The ledger binds each deposit to exactly one key, so identities named jetty, mirror, and crystal require three deposits. Each additional fake ties up another $100 and, at an assumed 12% simple annual borrowing rate, incurs about $0.99 in interest per lockup. Refunding the principal leaves financing as the recurring marginal cost of multiplying bidding identities.
